candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 22:1 (Abraham's final blessing (22:1)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And it came to pass in the first week in the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, that is, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the feast of weeks — that is, the feast of the first-fruits of the harvest — to Abraham, their father, and Abraham rejoiced because his two sons had come' — Jubilees preserves Abraham's celebration of the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot / Pentecost) in his final year, with BOTH Isaac and Ishmael in fellowship at the patriarchal altar. The Tewahedo Pentecost liturgy preserves a 'family-reunion-at-the-altar' theme: estranged-but-not-cursed branches of Abraham's seed gathered at the table. The Tewahedo's distinctive pastoral practice of welcoming Ishmaelite (Muslim) Ethiopian Christians-from-Muslim-families to communion-table preparation has its canonical Jubilees anchor here.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And he called Jacob and said: my son Jacob, may the God of all bless thee and strengthen thee to do righteousness, and His will before Him, and may He choose thee and thy seed that ye may become a people for His inheritance according to His will alway. And do thou, my son Jacob, remember my words, and observe the commandments of Abraham, thy father' — Abraham's final blessing of Jacob (his preferred grandson over Isaac's other line through Esau) directly anticipates the Jacob-not-Esau election preserved by Jubilees. The Tewahedo Jacobite-Israelite identification (the Tewahedo Church reads itself as the legitimate Israelite-Jacobite continuation, with the Solomonic dynasty as the canonical-political extension of the Davidic line through Menelik I as Solomon's son in the Kǝbrä Nägäśt tradition) finds its earliest canonical warrant in Abraham's direct-to-Jacob blessing here. The grandfather's blessing of Jacob over his father Isaac's potential to favor Esau is itself read as canonical priority-of-grace over inherited-order.

The Tewahedo's distinctive pastoral practice of welcoming Ishmaelite (Muslim) Ethiopian Christians-from-Muslim-families to communion-table preparation has its canonical Jubilees anchor here.

Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And he called Jacob and said: my son Jacob, may the God of all bless thee and strengthen thee to do righteousness, and His will before Him, and may He choose thee and thy seed that ye may become a people for His inheritance according to His will alway. And do thou, my son Jacob, remember my words, and observe the commandments of Abraham, thy father' — Abraham's final blessing of Jacob (his preferred grandson over Isaac's other line through Esau) directly anticipates the Jacob-not-Esau election preserved by Jubilees. The Tewahedo Jacobite-Israelite identification (the Tewahedo Church reads itself as the legitimate Israelite-Jacobite continuation, with the Solomonic dynasty as the canonical-political extension of the Davidic line through Menelik I as Solomon's son in the Kǝbrä Nägäśt tradition) finds its earliest canonical warrant in Abraham's direct-to-Jacob blessing here. The grandfather's blessing of Jacob over his father Isaac's potential to favor Esau is itself read as canonical priority-of-grace over inherited-order.
